lead: A truth table can be written as a sum of minterms or a product of maxterms. Both are exact and canonical: no simplification yet. A Karnaugh map redraws the truth table so cells that differ in one bit touch; grouping touching 1s removes the variables that change. The result is a cheaper SOP expression. Grouping 0s gives POS. This is used whenever a small logic function must become a few gates, as in adders, selectors and control logic.
prereq: You need: 5.2 Boolean algebra, logic gates and universal gates for truth tables and Boolean identities.

blocks.text: A product term is variables ANDed; a sum term is variables ORed. A minterm of n variables is a product term that contains every variable once, plain or complemented. A maxterm is a sum term that contains every variable once, plain or complemented. Number the row by reading the input bits as a binary number, A as MSB. In a minterm a 1 gives the plain variable and a 0 gives its complement. In a maxterm a 0 gives the plain variable and a 1 gives its complement. Minterm m<sub>i</sub> is 1 only on row i. Maxterm M<sub>i</sub> is 0 only on row i. For row 0101 (i = 5), m<sub>5</sub> = A'BC'D and M<sub>5</sub> = A + B' + C + D'.
F = Σ m<sub>i</sub> for rows with F = 1; F = Π M<sub>i</sub> for rows with F = 0
blocks.where: m<sub>i</sub> is the minterm numbered i; M<sub>i</sub> is the maxterm numbered i; Σ means OR of terms; Π means AND of terms; i runs over 0 to 2<sup>n</sup>−1.

items: Canonical SOP is the OR of all minterms where F = 1, written Σm(...).
Canonical POS is the AND of all maxterms where F = 0, written ΠM(...).
The two index lists are complements: if S is the minterm list, the maxterm list is every index from 0 to 2<sup>n</sup>−1 not in S.

blocks.text: The K-map is a truth table folded into a grid. Rows and columns follow Gray order 00, 01, 11, 10, so any two neighbouring cells differ in exactly one input bit. A 2-variable map has 4 cells; a 3-variable map has 8; a 4-variable map has 16. The edges wrap: top row touches bottom row, left column touches right column, and the four corners are mutually adjacent. A group must be a rectangle of 1, 2, 4, 8 or 16 cells — any power of two — never 3 or 6. So a 4-variable map with all sixteen cells at 1 can be taken as one block, giving the constant 1. Larger groups are better because each doubling removes one variable.

For SOP, group the 1s: a variable that is 1 in every cell of the group stays plain, one that is 0 in every cell stays complemented, and one that changes is dropped. Prime implicants are groups that cannot be made larger. Essential prime implicants cover a 1 that no other prime implicant covers. Don't-care cells, marked X, may be treated as 1 or 0 only when they enlarge a group. Some syllabi call the map a Veitch diagram.

SOP minimization is the main exam method: mark 1s, cover every 1 with the largest possible groups, and OR the terms. POS uses the same map but you group the 0s. Each group of 0s gives one sum term. A variable that is 0 in every cell of the group is written plain; a variable that is 1 in every cell is written complemented; a changing variable is omitted. AND the sum terms. Never complement the whole answer after grouping zeros. If 1s are fewer, SOP is shorter; if 0s are fewer, POS is shorter.

figure.caption: The four corner 1s form one group and the four middle 1s form another; each group removes the two variables that change.

spec.title: K-map for F(A,B,C,D) = Σm(0,2,5,7,8,10,13,15)
spec.aria: A 4 by 4 K-map whose columns are CD = 00, 01, 11, 10, with the four corner cells marked as one group and the four middle cells marked as a second group.

examples.question: Minimize F(A,B,C,D) = Σm(0,2,5,7,8,10,13,15) on a 4-variable K-map. Give the minimized SOP and POS forms. Show the groups and the literal rule.
steps: Write each minterm as a 4-bit code A B C D: m0 = 0000, m2 = 0010, m5 = 0101, m7 = 0111, m8 = 1000, m10 = 1010, m13 = 1101, m15 = 1111. Put 1 in these cells.
Group the corners m0, m2, m8, m10. In all four B = 0 and D = 0; A and C change. A fixed 0 gives a complemented literal in SOP, so the term is B'D'.
Group the middle four m5, m7, m13, m15. In all four B = 1 and D = 1; A and C change. The term is BD.
For POS, group the 0s. Group m1, m3, m9, m11: B = 0, D = 1, A and C change. In POS a fixed 0 gives the plain variable and a fixed 1 gives the complement, so the sum term is (B + D').
Group m4, m6, m12, m14: B = 1, D = 0, so the sum term is (B' + D). AND them: F = (B + D')(B' + D).
examples.answer: Minimized SOP is F = B'D' + BD; minimized POS is F = (B + D')(B' + D).

traps: Using row/column order 00, 01, 10, 11 instead of Gray 00, 01, 11, 10; then touching cells may differ in two bits.
Forgetting wrap-around: top-bottom, left-right and the four corners are adjacent.
In POS, copying the SOP literal rule. Grouping 0s: a 0 gives the plain variable, a 1 gives the complement.
Taking a group of 3 or 6 cells; only powers of two are legal.
Using a don't-care X to make a group that covers no 1 (SOP) or no 0 (POS); X is used only to enlarge an existing group.

quiz.q: Define minterm and maxterm for 3 variables.
quiz.a: A minterm is a product term with all three variables once, plain or complemented; it is 1 on exactly one row. A maxterm is a sum term with all three variables once; it is 0 on exactly one row.

quiz.q: Why does a K-map use Gray order 00, 01, 11, 10 for rows and columns?
quiz.a: So any two neighbouring cells differ in exactly one input bit. A group then removes only the variables that change.

quiz.q: Minimize F(A,B,C) = Σm(0,1,3,7) using a 3-variable K-map in SOP form.
quiz.a: Group m0,m1 → A'B'. Group m3,m7 → BC. Result: F = A'B' + BC.

quiz.q: For a 3-variable function F = ΠM(1,3,5,7), find the canonical SOP list and the minimized SOP.
quiz.a: The maxterm list gives zeros at 1,3,5,7, so the minterm list is 0,2,4,6. All these rows have C = 0, so F = C'.

quiz.q: Minimize F(A,B,C) = Σm(0,2,5,7) with don't-cares d(4,6) in SOP form.
quiz.a: Use the X at 4 and 6 in two groups. Group m0, m2, m4, m6: C = 0 in all four, A and B change, so the term is C'. Group m4, m5, m6, m7: A = 1 in all four, B and C change, so the term is A. Result: F = C' + A. It covers m0, m2, m5, m7 and covers no row that must be 0. If you group only m5, m7 you get the term AC, giving F = C' + AC.

quiz.q: Why can a don't-care cell not be grouped by itself?
quiz.a: A group of only X adds a term that is never required. X may be used only when it joins a group containing at least one needed 1 for SOP or one needed 0 for POS.

quiz.q: Write the canonical POS form for F(A,B) = Σm(0,2).
quiz.a: The missing indices are 1 and 3, so F = ΠM(1,3) = (A + B')(A' + B').

beyond: Not for the exam. Real logic synthesis replaces pencil K-maps with Quine-McCluskey and Espresso algorithms, then maps the result onto look-up tables inside an FPGA. The same grouping idea survives as the prime-implicant step in those tools. Search for 'Quine-McCluskey method', 'Espresso logic minimizer' and 'FPGA LUT truth table'.
